name: Moss Grey
lede: Moss Grey is a muted greenish grey, a color defined by the old RAL system and the ISCC-NBS names.

sections.title: A greeny-grey
sections.body:
Paterson defines moss-grey simply as a greeny-grey [1]. The swatch here is documented twice: as RAL 7003 in the German RAL system, dated 1927 in our sources, and as a color in the 1955 ISCC-NBS lists, block 109, where the name is "light olive gray" at 5.3 CIEDE2000 units away [2]. The Maerz and Paul dictionary of 1930 is cited as a source by the ISCC-NBS circular [2]. RAL values on screen are approximate [2].

Its neighbors are [[moss-green]], a more yellow-green color, and [[slate-grey]]; the nearest name in our learning set is taupe, 9.3 away [2][1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our 23,781-painting archive a color near it appears in 1,516 paintings, 6.37% of the total, more often than 88% of the named colors, as photographed [3]. Among 795 paintings where the within-painting lens finds it, it most often plays a light [3]. It is most devoted to Jacob Isaacksz van Ruisdael, in 6 of his 18 works here [3]. As a printed phrase, *moss grey* peaks in the 1850s [4]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so read them as screen colors [3].
